injuries.injury: Traore will be re-evaluated in approximately 8-10 weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injuries.detail: Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
injuries.detail: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

injuries.injury: Williams (hamstring) won't play Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
injuries.detail: Williams will miss a second consecutive game due to right hamstring injury management. Royce O'Neale and Tidjane Salaun should continue to see more minutes off the bench for Charlotte.

injuries.injury: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
injuries.detail: Allen is set to miss a third consecutive contest due to a concussion. Sion James will continue to start while Royce O'Neale should get more minutes off the bench.

injuries.injury: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
injuries.detail: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

injuries.injury: Kalkbrenner has been ruled out for the rest of Monday's game against Memphis due to left hip soreness. He'll end with two rebounds in nine minutes.
injuries.detail: Hannes Steinbach could see additional opportunities as the backup center with Kalkbrenner shut down for the rest of the night. The Creighton product can be considered day-to-day moving forward.

injuries.injury: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

injuries.injury: Smith (illness) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Hornets.
injuries.detail: Smith has been a regular on the injury report recently due to a gastrointestinal illness, though he played in Chicago's last two outings, averaging 18.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.0 combined steals-plus-blocks in 29.5 minutes per contest over that brief stretch. If the big man is unable to play Wednesday, Nic Claxton would likely enter the first unit.

injuries.injury: Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
injuries.detail: Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
injuries.detail: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

injuries.injury: Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
injuries.detail: Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.injury: Head coach Steve Kerr said Monday that Williams (hamstring) is on track to return Wednesday against the Kings, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.detail: Williams hasn't played since Nov. 9 due to a left hamstring strain, though he could return to action as soon as Wednesday. The Warriors will provide an update on his status by Tuesday night, and if the 27-year-old is cleared to return, there would be fewer minutes available for guys like Gary Payton, LJ Cryer and Will Richard.

injuries.injury: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

injuries.injury: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
injuries.detail: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

injuries.injury: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

injuries.injury: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

injuries.injury: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
injuries.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

injuries.injury: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injuries.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

injuries.injury: Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.detail: The rookie standout has been diagnosed with a moderate-grade ankle sprain, and he'll be sidelined for at least the next month or so. It's a tough blow for an upstart Grizzlies team, which will now rely even more heavily on Ty Jerome's playmaking for the foreseeable future. Taylor Hendricks has a chance to nail down a consistent role off the bench as well.

injuries.injury: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
injuries.detail: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

injuries.injury: Grant was diagnosed with a grade 1 left calf strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
injuries.detail: Grant suffered the injury during Thursday's 126-98 victory over Golden State. He will now be sidelined for at least two weeks, with the team expected to provide an update on his condition at that time. While Grant is on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Kris Murray are candidates for more minutes.

injuries.injury: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

injuries.injury: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
injuries.detail: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

injuries.injury: Antetokounmpo (groin) participated in most of Tuesday's practice, Zachary Weinberger of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.detail: Antetokounmpo is trending in the right direction after missing Sunday's win over the Thunder with a groin injury. If the superstar forward returns to action in Wednesday's game against Philadelphia, there would be fewer minutes available for guys like Bobby Portis, Nikola Jovic and Andrew Wiggins.

injuries.injury: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injuries.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injuries.injury: DiVincenzo (Achilles) has been cleared for team basketball activities and is targeting a return to game action in January, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injuries.detail: DiVincenzo suffered a ruptured right Achilles in late April but is seemingly ahead of schedule in his recovery. With the veteran guard and Anthony Edwards (knee) both sidelined, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon figure to continue seeing increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
injuries.detail: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

injuries.injury: Clarkson (foot) didn't participate in Tuesday's practice, Jared Schwartz of the New York Post reports.
injuries.detail: Clarkson has hit the inactive list in each of New York's last two games due to plantar fasciitis in his right foot. If he remains out Wednesday against Cleveland, Landry Shamet and Pacome Dadiet would be candidates for more minutes, especially if OG Anunoby (calf) or Miles McBride (adductor) is ruled out.

injuries.injury: McBride (groin) practiced Tuesday, per Jared Schwartz of the New York Post.
injuries.detail: McBride is progressing well from left adductor tightness. The Knicks will reveal later Tuesday if the guard carries an injury designation into Wednesday's game against Cleveland.

injuries.injury: Anunoby (calf) did not participate in Tuesday's practice, Jared Schwartz of the New York Post reports.
injuries.detail: Anunoby has missed two straight games with a left calf issue, and it's not encouraging to see him sit out Tuesday's practice ahead of Wednesday's game against Cleveland. If the 29-year-old forward remains sidelined, Pacome Dadiet, Mohamed Diawara and Landry Shamet would be candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Mara (shin) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers.
injuries.detail: Mara will miss a second consecutive contest due to a right shin contusion, with his next opportunity to play coming against Minnesota on Wednesday. With the rookie big man sidelined, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy are candidates for increased playing time.

injuries.injury: Caruso (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers, according to the NBA's official injury report.
injuries.detail: Caruso will miss his second consecutive game as Oklahoma City continues managing his right hip injury. His absence further depletes the Thunder's backcourt, potentially creating additional opportunities for Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain.

injuries.injury: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injuries.detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injuries.injury: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injuries.detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injuries.injury: Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers, according to the NBA's official injury report.
injuries.detail: Williams remains sidelined following left ankle surgery, with no confirmed return date. His continued absence leaves Oklahoma City without a key offensive contributor, allowing additional opportunities for the Thunder's remaining perimeter players.

injuries.injury: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers
injuries.detail: Williams returned from a seven-game absence to make two appearances before sitting out Sunday against Miami. His recurring back issues leave Oklahoma City's depleted frontcourt even thinner, potentially opening additional minutes for Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy.

injuries.injury: Topic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers, according to the NBA's official injury report.
injuries.detail: Topic will miss his third consecutive game due to a left hip strain. The rookie has averaged just 11.3 minutes across three appearances this season, so his absence should have minimal fantasy implications despite Oklahoma City's depleted backcourt.

injuries.injury: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
injuries.detail: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

injuries.injury: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injuries.injury: Embiid (illness) is out for Monday's game against Portland, Austin Krell of OnPattison.com reports.
injuries.detail: The star big man can be considered day-to-day moving forward. With Embiid sidelined Monday, Dominick Barlow is a candidate to start at center for the 76ers while Adem Bona (back) helps pick up the slack off the bench.

injuries.injury: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

injuries.injury: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
injuries.detail: Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

injuries.injury: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
injuries.detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

injuries.injury: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

injuries.injury: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.detail: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

injuries.injury: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injuries.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injuries.injury: Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
injuries.detail: Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.injury: Fox (shin) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Kings, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
injuries.detail: Fox will miss his second outing of the regular season due to a right shin contusion. Stephon Castle will operate as the primary ballhandler with Dylan Harper (hip) also sidelined, while Jordan McLaughlin should see increased burn off the Spurs' bench.

injuries.injury: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.detail: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

injuries.injury: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injuries.detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injuries.injury: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
injuries.detail: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

injuries.injury: Wembanyama (back) won't play Monday against the Kings, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
injuries.detail: Wembanyama is dealing with some back pain and will sit out Monday's game against the 1-14 Kings, but he's expected to return for Wednesday's NBA Cup game in Portland. Luka Kornet will likely get the start with Wembanyama unavailable, and Stephon Castle should see a sizeable uptick in usage.
